the full pipeline. Manual Retry-proof button on failed tracker cards only -
no auto-resume, no parallel writers. Retries are offered only once the
payout tx hash is known; a burn whose agent never pays has nothing to
attest.

fix(tee): recover enclave after Railway redeploy, retire old sender

generates a fresh keypair and wipes the sealed key from memory. Recovery

  dead enclave. This had to precede the re-seal: updateKey routes through
  the same selector, so ciphertext addressed to the orphan is lost with no
  revert and the fee spent. Two updateKey calls were lost that way on
  2026-08-06.

- re-seal the SAME key, so dropSigner, settler, and scoreSigner all stay
  0x5e8BfFA9... and no contract needed rewiring. Proven by minting tokenId
  31 and recovering the enclave signature to dropSigner.

fix(fdc): read the DA proof shape the layer actually returns

The proof lookup pointed at `proof-by-request-round-raw`, which returns
`{response_hex, attestation_type, proof}` — the attestation as a single
ABI-encoded blob. `toFdcProof` expects the field-by-field struct, and
looked for the Merkle nodes under `merkleProof` where the DA layer sends
`proof`. It failed the `Array.isArray` guard and returned null.

`pollForFdcProof` reported that null identically to a timeout, so a proof
that had already finalized surfaced as "FDC proof did not finalize within
the polling window". The console 404s were a red herring: the proof route
maps "round not final yet" to 404 by design, and the round in question
finalized normally.

Switch to `proof-by-request-round`, whose response is the decoded struct
`toFdcProof` already maps, and accept the Merkle nodes under either key.

fix(redeem): add missing topic2_3_opr to payout log filter

The payout watcher queried the explorer with three topics but only two
pairwise operators. The API requires an operator for every pair, so it
rejected the request with `status: '0'` and
`"Required query parameters missing: topic2_3_opr"` instead of filtering.

The rejection arrives as HTTP 200 with no `result` array, which the poll
loop could not distinguish from "the agent has not paid yet". Every
redemption therefore sat on "Waiting for agent payout" for the full
15-minute window and then reported a payout that had, in fact, already
settled on-chain.

Confirmed against redemption 43907492 for 0xe9eE885c…3626: six
`RedemptionPerformed` events existed the whole time. With the third
operator the query returns the log and the watch advances to `agent-paid`.

Also treat a `status: '0'` response other than "No logs found" as a hard
failure. A malformed query cannot become well-formed by waiting, so
surfacing it beats spending the window on a request that can never
succeed.

feat(leaderboard): gate score submission behind a server attestation

An open `submitScore` let anyone write any number to the leaderboard. This
closes that path by requiring an ECDSA attestation from a server-held signer.

The contract gains `submitScoreWithProof`, a `scoreSigner` the owner can
re-point, and single-use `usedRunNonces`. While a signer is set, the legacy
`submitScore` reverts, so an unattested score cannot be recorded at all;
clearing the signer to zero reopens it, which is the rollback. The digest binds
to (contract, chainId, player, score, ship, nonce), so an attestation is
worthless on another deployment or from another wallet, and a rejected
submission does not burn the nonce.

Two routes carry the off-chain half. `/api/game/start` issues a run token
bound to (contract, chainId, player, nonce, issuedAt) — proof the server
minted the nonce, with no server-side session state. `/api/game/submit-score`
verifies that token, bounds the score against elapsed time, and only then
signs. It deliberately does not replay the run: 14 unseeded `Math.random()`
calls make the simulation non-reproducible, so this is an availability-bias
signer rather than TEE replay. A plausible-but-bounded fabricated run still
passes, and that limit is documented at the route.

The client requests a token at craft selection, so `issuedAt` brackets actual
play rather than page load.

Phase 2: FDC attestation client service and redemption status store

src/services/fdc.ts — the attestation round-trip, one function per step:
  fetchFdcPrepareRequest  → verifier gives abiEncodedRequest
  requestFdcAttestation   → FdcHub.requestAttestation, reads back block ts
  fetchVotingRoundId      → Relay maps that timestamp to a round
  pollForFdcProof         → DA layer until finalized (404 = retry)
  verifyPayoutOnChain     → PixelOrbitRedemptionProof.verifyPayout
  isPayoutProven          → cheap read for already-proven redemptions

Two details that would otherwise bite:
- The DA layer sends every uint as a decimal string. viem refuses to
  encode a string where the ABI says uint256, so toFdcProof() coerces
  the whole tuple once instead of at the call site.
- The voting round comes from the request tx's block timestamp, not
  from anything the caller picks — so the receipt's block is read back
  before Relay can resolve the round.

src/hooks/useRedemptionStatus.ts — module-level Map + useSyncExternalStore,
matching useNow's pattern. Module-level because the attestation outlives
the modal that started it: closing RedeemFxrpModal unmounts the component
while FDC is still minutes out, and the progress has to survive that.
Snapshot is cached so Object.is bail-out works and does not loop.

was offered a Reclaim Asset button that could only revert with

feat: replace the NEW BIDS badge with the state that actually needs the pilot

"NEW BIDS" only ever described one thing, and not the one worth surfacing: a
sealed bid on an open auction is not a to-do, while a payable win, a refundable
bond and an auction waiting on the enclave all are — and none of them showed up
on the profile at all. The badge also spoke only for the seller, because
PilotProfile had userListings but never loaded userBids.

Rank every open state across both sides and show the top one. The ordering lives
in a PRIORITY array rather than nested conditionals so a new state cannot quietly
bury an existing one, and money the user can lose outranks money they can
collect, which outranks a call that unblocks everyone else, which outranks news.
The ping dot is now gated on actionable, so it fires for a transaction and stays
quiet for a notification.

Seller states mirror the contract rather than guessing: reclaim is withheld
during the PAYMENT_WINDOW grace and reopens after, matching reclaimUnsettled and
ItemActionPanel's own gating. There is deliberately no completed-sale alert —
paying zeroes the winner's bond and the listing leaves userListings entirely, so
claiming "sold" would outlive the data behind it.

fix(marketplace): reclaim button respects settlement window, bidders can settle

Two bugs in the auction endgame, both from the UI disagreeing with the
contract about what state a closed auction is in.

Reclaim Asset stayed visible in My Listings once an auction ended with
bids but before settlement. The button was gated only on `winner !== ''`,
but a closed-and-unsettled auction has no winner yet, so it rendered and
`reclaimUnsettled` reverted with "Settlement still possible" — the
contract refuses to let a seller pull an auction out from under bidders
whose bonds are locked.

The gate mirrors the contract's own window rather than just testing
bidCount, because that block is temporary. PAYMENT_WINDOW past the close
with still no verdict, `reclaimUnsettled` opens back up — the escape
hatch for an enclave that never answers. Hiding reclaim permanently would
have stranded the NFT in exactly the case the hatch exists for. During
the grace the seller is not stuck either: Settle Auction is already

The TEE public key is not on-chain — the machine registry exposes only
addresses and host URLs — so it comes from the proxy's /info endpoint,
the same way the reference sealing tool reads it. That makes the proxy

feat(fassets): replace reservation minting with direct minting via Xaman

The reservation flow could not be completed with the wallets available. It
needs the FAssets payment reference in the XRPL Memos[0].Memo.MemoData field
as raw hex; GemWallet and Crossmark only expose a "notes" box, which is a
different field, and their destination tag caps at 10 digits — a 32-byte
reference fits in neither. Verified against the FDC verifier: a text memo
yields standardPaymentReference 0x000...0, so the agent can never match the
payment.

Direct minting removes the constraint rather than working around it. The
payment goes to the Core Vault with a memo naming the Flare recipient, and an
off-chain executor finalises the mint. Confirmed live on Coston2:
directMintingPaymentAddress resolves, and DirectMintingExecuted fires roughly
every 3 minutes from executor 0x103b3840.

What this changes for the user:

  - any amount, not 10-FXRP lots (lotSize rounding is gone)
  - no collateral reservation fee — nothing is spent on Flare at all
  - no payment deadline, so no way to forfeit a fee by being slow
  - no manual FDC attestation step; two signatures become one

Fees read from chain: 0.25% minting (floor 0.1 FXRP) plus a 0.1 executor fee,
deducted from what is sent. The net mint is found by binary search because the
minting fee is a function of the net amount, not the gross — subtracting a
known fee would be wrong.

Xaman is used for the payment because it accepts a full transaction template,
so the memo is set by the app rather than typed. Its API secret stays
server-side behind two proxy routes, matching the existing api/fdc pattern.

Completion is observed via the recipient's FXRP balance, not a receipt: the
executor sends that transaction, not us. A timeout reports "still minting"
rather than a failure — the payment is already attested and will complete.

Tier 1.1c. The redeem half of the FAssets round trip already existed; this
adds the mint half, so FXRP can be created in-app rather than assuming the
user arrives holding some. Service layer only — no UI yet.

src/services/mint.ts implements the five-step flow:
  1. quoteMint reads lotSize, collateralReservationFee and the agent list
     fresh, picks the cheapest usable agent (status NORMAL, enough free lots,
     most free collateral as tiebreak) and prices the XRPL payment.
  2. reserveMint calls reserveCollateral, passing the quoted feeBIPS as
     _maxMintingFeeBIPS so the tx reverts rather than silently paying more if
     the agent raised its fee since the quote.
  3. the caller shows the payment instructions; the user pays on the XRPL.
  4. executeMint attests that payment via FDC and
  5. calls executeMinting with the proof.

The reservation is persisted to localStorage the moment it is decoded, before
anything is displayed. The CR fee (~1.72 C2FLR) is spent and non-refundable
at that point, so a closed tab must not lose the payment address, reference
or deadline — without those the user cannot finish or even identify the
reservation. It is cleared only after the FXRP exists.

transaction, and handing the user someone else's paymentAddress would send
their XRP to the wrong agent.

~90s but finalization lags, and timing out is recoverable since the
reservation stays valid until the underlying deadline.

Two new server routes proxy FDC because the browser cannot reach it — the
verifier requires an X-API-KEY and neither service sends CORS headers.

fix(marketplace): wait for read node to catch up before refreshing

A new auction listing did not appear in the marketplace until a reload,
while a cancel on the same listing showed up immediately.

waitForTransactionReceipt only proves some node saw the transaction. The
public Coston2 endpoint is load balanced, so the follow-up eth_call could
land on a peer still behind and answer from pre-transaction state.

That asymmetry is why only new listings broke: fetchAllListings reads
getListingCount() first and loops up to that value, so a stale count hides
the new id entirely. A cancel or price change sits at an id inside the loop
regardless, so any single fresh read surfaces it.

Each write now passes its receipt's blockNumber to revalidateMarketData,
which polls eth_blockNumber (cacheTime: 0, since viem memoises it per
client) until the node has caught up, then reads and writes both caches.

fix: chunk getLogs to respect Coston2 RPC block limit

Coston2 RPC limits eth_getLogs to 30 blocks per request. Replaced
single 'earliest'->'latest' query with chunked fetching: scan last
100k blocks in 5k-block chunks. Gracefully skips failed chunks.

fix: replace metaMaskWallet with injectedWallet to fix MetaMask connection

metaMaskWallet relies on EIP-6963 rdns discovery which fails when
HashPack extension interferes. injectedWallet uses window.ethereum
directly, bypassing EIP-6963 and connecting to whatever wallet is
actually injected.
